rowdata.pxWarningMessage: This activity has more than 25 steps. Consider decomposing this activity into smaller, more modular pieces.

Use of the WriteNow option in the Obj-Save ,Obj-Delete activity methods interferes with the PRPC transaction model and may result in stale database records. Consider allowing PRPC to commit the record when the transaction completes.

Using Obj-Save skips common processing such as validation, history creation, and setting last update data. For updating data instances, use a savable Data Page. For updating cases use normal flow processing. For advanced usages, such as updating cases or data during agent processing, use activity APIs such as Save or UpdateWorkObject.

Use of the Commit activity method interferes with the PRPC transaction model and may result in stale database records. Consider removing; In most cases, PRPC already does a commit at the end of the transaction.

When acquiring a lock using Obj-Open or Obj-Refresh-And-Lock you should always check to make sure the lock was actually granted. This is commonly done using StepStatusFail in the transition of the step acquiring the lock or in the precondition of the step immediately after the lock is acquired.
The use of activity rules should be limited. The need for activities can be reduced by using data transforms, as well as techniques such as case management, the Engine API, and declaratives.
The call to activity 'InsertDokumenPNC' contains the AppliesTo class name 'ASM-FW-GCNMFW-Work-PNC'. Consider defining a step page of that AppliesTo class in the activity call instead.
You should create a test case for this rule to identify any regression issues that might occur when this rule is modified.
